title: Exchange-Traded Funds and the Wash Sale Loophole
authors: Michael Dambra; Andrew Glover; Charles M.C. Lee; Phillip J. Quinn
eligible_reason: The ETF-level analysis (Table 2, Figure 1) is a staggered binary design: an incumbent index ETF becomes 'washable' (peer = 1) in the month a 99%-return-correlated ETF is introduced, at ETF-specific dates, with never-treated ETFs as controls and always-treated ETFs dropped. But it is estimated only as a stacked DiD: cohorts by treatment month with +/-36-month windows, never-treated controls appended per cohort, FE cohortXetf and cohortXdate, cluster focal ETF (ETF_Level_Analysis.do lines 205-304). Columns 2 and 4 add time-varying controls (spread volatility size bh_ret_12 and return interactions). The filer-level regressions use ts1 (tax-sensitive institution indicator), a cross-sectional characteristic, not a staggered treatment. No unstacked TWFE is reported. Shipped data are pseudo samples with altered values.
design_notes: Code: ETF_Level_Analysis.do (338 lines; Tables 1A and 2, Figure 1), Filer_Level_Analysis.do (606 lines; Tables 1B, 1C, 3-8), SAS_WhaleWisdom_DataPrep.sas, MinimumWashingLoop.do, HeartbeatTrades.do, AncernoIllustration.do (Figure 2). ETF panel: CRSP monthly index ETFs 1993-2022 (focal = cusip8 group), monthly; washable_date = first month a >=0.99 correlated partner ETF exists; peer = washable flag carried forward (equals treat x post, confirmed by the code's corr check); always-treated ETFs dropped (always==1), never_treated = never washable. Stacking: event1 = first month peer switches to 1; group1 = cohort by event date; for each cohort keep treated ETFs with eventtime in [-36,36] and never-treated ETFs (peer==0) over the same dates; append; cohortXetf = group(cohort focal), cohortXdate = group(cohort date). Table 2: reghdfe lnvol peer if spread!=. & volatility!=., a(cohortXetf cohortXdate) cl(focal) (col 1); reghdfe lnvol peer spread volatility size bh_ret_12 c.bh_ret_12#treat c.bh_ret_12#post c.bh_ret_12#peer, a(cohortXetf cohortXdate) cl(focal) (col 2); same for ln_shrout (cols 3-4). Figure 1: standardized treated-control differences by event time. Filer-level: reghdfe <outcome> ts1 [controls], a(year qtr) or a(filer_id year), $cl cluster.
estimators_reported: stacked_did_twfe (reghdfe, cohort x ETF and cohort x month FE; Table 2)
main_or_robustness: main for the ETF-level evidence (Table 2); the paper's headline results are filer-level
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Cohorts are months of first 99%-correlated peer introduction (1993-2022); count not recoverable from the 5% pseudo sample.

specs.exclusion_reason: stacked design (cohort x ETF, cohort x date FE)
specs.outcome: lnvol (log monthly share volume, adjusted, winsorized)
specs.treatment_var: peer (= treat x post; washable ETF indicator)
specs.treatment_definition: incumbent index ETF has at least one ETF with >=0.99 monthly return correlation trading, from the first such month onward
specs.controls: none (col 1); spread volatility size bh_ret_12 c.bh_ret_12#treat c.bh_ret_12#post c.bh_ret_12#peer (col 2)
specs.sample_condition: spread!=. & volatility!=.; eventtime in [-36, 36]; always-treated dropped
specs.data_file: event_time_data built from final_99 (anon_crspmonthly.dta + anon_sbfusmfd.dta pseudo inputs)

specs.exclusion_reason: ts1 is a cross-sectional tax-sensitivity classification, not a treatment that switches on; many columns add controls and interactions
specs.outcome: unique_etfs_hc_w, etf_intensity_hc_w, ln_swaps_w, plr_w, plr_etf_hc_w, hb_*_intensity_w
specs.fe: none, a(filer_id), a(year qtr), or a(year filer_id)

data_provenance: synthetic (README: ~5% pseudo datasets with anonymized identifiers and changed values and dates; will not produce the coefficients in the tables; Ancerno data cannot be shared)
data_files: ExampleData/sas_ww_illustration.sas7bdat, sas_crsp_illustration.sas7bdat, anon_identifiers.dta, anon_complete_collapsed.dta, anon_fadv_allyears_sm.dta, anon_busheeclassification.dta, anon_mgrno_cik_link.dta, anon_fundflows.dta (filer-level pseudo inputs)
screener_notes: Article text not available; table numbers from the do-file comments and README. The ETF-level design would qualify if estimated unstacked (binary peer indicator, ETF-specific adoption months, never-treated controls), but only stacked estimates are reported and the full CRSP-based panel is not shipped.
